unresolved.problem: The prompt asks why the nut got warm 'even though it did not move'. The exemplar says friction converted muscular energy to heat but never explains how friction heats a nut that shows d = 0. Section 2 and Section 5 say no work was done on the nut in that row (W = 0). The exemplar omits the Lesson 4 mechanism, which is microscopic relative movement and deformation at the spanner-nut and nut-bolt thread contacts. As written, the exemplars contradict each other: no work is done, yet friction does work and makes heat. The exemplar should add that small slipping or deformation occurs, so work against friction is not zero at the contacts even though the nut shows no visible displacement.
